newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French 10-year bond futures and three-month interest rate futures sprinted ahead on Tuesday on market relief at the government's deficit-cutting package which analysts said was bullish for European monetary union.
The market was also lifted by the firmness of U.S. T-bonds ahead of testimony by Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony due at 1800 GMT.
"Overall the market is looking good after the public finance audit. Europe is going to happen. The euro is back on track," said a senior trader.
The September 10-year bond future settled up 0.48 at 130.70.
September PIBOR ended seven points higher at 96.57, helped by a strong showing by the franc which rose more than a third of a centime against the mark to trade at 3.3687 late in the day.
Ten-year government bonds (OATs) outperformed their German counterparts with the negative spread widening to minus 15 from minus 13.
One analyst said the bond future could retest its contract high of 130.88, and breach 131 on Wednesday.
Another trader agreed with the optimistic outlook, on the condition there was no bad news from Greenspan's testimony to Congress suggesting that the Fed might raise rates in the near future.
Traders said the franc was being helped by investor worries about the Germany's ability to meet the Maastricht treaty criteria for a single currency.
"I'm covering my clients aginst a fall in the mark and aaginst a rise in the dollar," said one foreign exchange operator.
Another trader said that the market was being supported by French institutional buying which always buys on dips.
"That's contribhuting to its strength," he said, adding that, "speculative non-resident funds are long on the French market."
